guarantees.claim: in_valid, out_ready, crypt, dec_key_gen, crypt_q, dec_key_gen_q, sub_bytes_out_req, key_expand_out_req are each directly assigned to the corresponding bit of sp2v_sig_chk (bits 0 through 7).
sp_enc_err is the logical OR of the entire sp2v_sig_err vector and the input sp_enc_err_i, asserting high whenever any encoding error is detected locally or elsewhere in the core.

assumptions.claim: sp2v_sig_chk must correctly decode the sparse signals into valid logical 0/1 values; the decoded control outputs are used without further local validation.
assumptions.risk: Corrupted cipher operation due to wrong control signal states (e.g., incorrect valid/ready/crypt mode).

assumptions.claim: sp2v_sig_err must reliably assert a non-zero value whenever the sparse checker detects an encoding error, so that sp_enc_err is raised.
assumptions.cond: when a sparse encoding error occurs
assumptions.risk: Encoding errors may be missed, masking security-critical faults.

assumptions.claim: sp_enc_err_i must correctly accumulate encoding errors from other parts of the cipher core and be stable in time so that sp_enc_err accurately reflects the total error state.
assumptions.risk: Undetected errors could propagate silently, potentially leading to silent data corruption or security violations.

assumptions.claim: When cfg_valid_i is asserted, op_i must be one of CIPH_FWD or CIPH_INV; no other values are allowed.
assumptions.risk: An invalid operation mode could cause undefined cipher behavior, possibly exposing secret data or breaking integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: The assertion AesCiphOpValid restricts op_i to only CIPH_FWD and CIPH_INV when cfg_valid_i is high. It is unclear whether other operation codes are legal under different cfg_valid_i conditions or if these two are exhaustive.
uncertain_points.risk: If other legal modes exist, the assertion would produce false violations; if a malicious or erroneous invalid mode appears outside cfg_valid_i, it could be accepted by downstream logic.

uncertain_points.claim: sp_enc_err_i is an external error signal; the relative timing of its update versus sp2v_sig_err is unknown. A temporal mismatch could cause sp_enc_err to miss an error or glitch.
uncertain_points.risk: An encoding error could be momentarily missed or a spurious error pulse could propagate, affecting error handling logic.

uncertain_points.claim: sp2v_sig_chk bits are used directly as control signals without any glitch-filtering or qualification. The checker's output stability must be guaranteed by the sparse checker instantiation elsewhere.
uncertain_points.risk: Transient glitches on decoded signals could cause false control events, leading to state machine hazards or data corruption.
